title: Focus window — review notes & micro-PR plan
body:
Goal: get one 1–2 file micro-PR merged in a single focused 90–120 minute window. Reduce context-switch overhead and leave a clear follow-up backlog.

Why this doc: been losing momentum juggling infra/serving-runtime reviews. Trying a compact ritual: a focused window with a checklist, quick heuristics, and a tiny post-merge followup plan. Notes for future me and anyone who wants to steal this flow.

Before the window (10–15m prep)
- Open the diff and the linked CI (PR-3214). skim to map change surface area: files changed, import churn, config/global flags.
- Find the minimal runtime-impacting lines (search for kv_cache, batching, kernel selection). If >3 files touch runtime core, consider splitting.
- Run quick local smoke to ensure reproducible failure: 
  - git checkout -b tmp/review-quick PR-3214
  - ./dev/run-mini-smoke --model=llama2 --seq=128
  - tail -n 200 logs/dev-smoke.log
- Gather related tickets: JIRA-RI-984 (kv cache edgecases), linked confluence page. Note any security signoffs required.

Focus window checklist (90–120m)
1) Safety and correctness (30–40m)
  - Read all changed tests first. If tests are missing for a behavioral change, add a minimal test.
  - Edgecase probe: identify 3 worst-case inputs (long seq, empty prompt, truncated kv). Manually run them against new code locally. Record outputs.
  - Data-sensitive changes: add note for security review if code touches telemetry or user content paths.
2) Readability and intent (15–25m)
  - Is the intent described at top of the file or in PR description? If not, request/patch a 2–3 line explanation.
  - Name hygiene: function/variable names should communicate stateful cache semantics. If variable name ambiguous, propose a rename inline.
3) Performance/regression risk (20–30m)
  - Spot synchronous loops or per-request allocations. Flag with comment like: // PERF: consider object reuse.
  - If quantization flags or kernel selection changed, run the small perf harness: 
      tools/perf/harness --model=resnet-ish --iter=500 --batch=1
  - If perf diff >10% in harness, request a perf note or revert to safe path.
4) Tests and CI (10–15m)
  - Ensure unit tests cover both happy path and at least one edge. If CI flakiness observed, add a local repro section in PR.
  - Mark any flaky test with TODO and a JIRA ticket (e.g., JIRA-RI-1002).
5) Merge readiness & rollout plan (5–10m)
  - If change touches runtime kernel selection, require canary: dedicated small % in Dedicated pool or staged rollout. Add rollout instructions in PR description.
  - Decide whether to merge or split into micro-PRs. If splitting: create folllow-up PR titles and minimal diffs.

Quick heuristics I use when in a hurry:
- If change is <= 10 LOC in hot path: require bench harness pass + one unit test.
- If change touches config toggles: must have a default-preserving migration.
- If change adds a boolean flag: prefer an enum with clear modes and comments.

Common micro-refactors to prefer over big rewrites (these are quick actions to take during window)
- Extract a small helper and call it from original spot (one file). Avoid moving files.
- Rename a misleading variable and update 2 uses.
- Add an opt-in flag behind existing config instead of flipping default semantics.

Example inline review language (fast comments)
- "nit: rename -> cacheWindowMs to avoid ambiguous units"
- "question: why return Optional here instead of empty list? prefer consistent types across API"
- "perf: this allocs per-request, consider pooling with thread_local buffer. see tools/perf/harness"

Manual test commands to keep handy
- run minimal smoke: ./dev/run-mini-smoke --config=local --seed=42
- run unit subset: pytest tests/serving/test_kv_cache.py::test_eviction_edgecase -q
- perf harness: tools/perf/harness --model=llama2 --iter=200 --batch=1

Post-merge immediate followups (write into PR before merging)
- Create a follow-up kanban card (label: followup-micro-pr) with items: add extra unit test, add perf note, file rename backlog.
- Add rollout steps and rollback checklist to PR description.
- Leave a brief summary comment describing what was intentionally left for later.

Followup backlog template (to paste into JIRA/notes)
- RI-XXXX: add deterministic test for truncated-kv case (owner: Danya, est: 2h)
- RI-XXXX: bench full-model with quantized kernel (owner: Evan, est: 3h)
- RI-XXXX: rename cacheWindowMs -> cacheWindowMillis across serving runtime (owner: Mira, est: 1h)

Notes to self / decisions made during today's window:
- Split out the config migration logic into follow-up PR. Too much surface for this window.
- Left a TODO to add a deterministic seed to perf harness to reduce flakiness. File ticket JIRA-RI-1009.
- Decided to preserve current default for dedicated pool routing; will propose canary post-merge.

Open questions / unresolved
- Does telemetry path need an opt-out attribute for private deployments? (check with security).
- Should cache eviction expose soft metrics (fast counters) or is that extra noise for SRE?

If this was helpful, adopt the ritual: set a timer, block slack for the window, and aim to leave the PR in a merged or clearly-split state with a 3-item follow-up backlog.

Misc quick notes (brain dump)
- Keep hot-path diffs small. When in doubt, split three ways: (1) correctness/test, (2) performance, (3) cleanup. Merge 1 first.
- Don't gate merge on docs for tiny behaviour fixes; instead create doc-ticket and link.
- Reuse this doc: copy into PR description checklist for micro-PRs.

-- Danya
